name: c-scenario-workspace
prompt: Edit only the central request journey diagram in this dashboard mockup. Preserve header, sidebar, all text outside the diagram, counters, button, colors, typography and overall layout exactly. Correct the network flow: the outgoing "Request sent" line must run ALL THE WAY from the left monitor to the right server, with its arrowhead arriving at the server, not stopping at the center X. Put this outgoing successful arrow on an upper horizontal lane. Under it, a separate return lane goes from the right server toward the left monitor, labelled "Reply (not received)", with the return line interrupted in the middle by the existing X "Reply lost"; dashed line on the left side of the interruption and left-pointing arrowhead at the monitor. Two clearly separated lanes, one successfully delivered request and one lost return reply. Keep "Your screen" and its "Unconfirmed" status, "Server" with "Saved" and "Pump inspection". Align cleanly within the existing diagram region with no text overlaps. Do not change anything else.
initialPrompt:
Create a polished high-fidelity desktop web dashboard mockup for the existing "Idempotent requests lab". Landscape 1536x1024. This is a static DESIGN PROPOSAL, not evidence of a running application. Use the supplied screenshot ONLY as a reference for navy ink, cobalt actions, flat white/cool-gray surfaces, and readable Atkinson Hyperlegible-style sans typography. Completely replace its page composition and excessive copy. Do not carry over its hero, paragraphs, explanatory footer, large duplicated headings or split-panel card arrangement. Preserve the functional premise: a fictional maintenance request was actually saved by the server, but its reply was lost; the user's next action is retrying the SAME request, which must not create another job. Display precisely the current lost-reply stage, BEFORE retry: one send, one saved request, no client confirmation. Short English labels only, no lorem ipsum, no fake charts, no statistics unrelated to this experiment, no avatars, no marketing, no photorealistic objects, no decorative illustrations, no 3D, no gradients. Deliberate typography, generous but useful spacing, crisp restrained line icons, accessible dark text, compact calm chrome, one blue primary action. Make an implementable premium product UI, full app viewport with no device frame. Show a clear separate "Technical controls" tab. All status colors have text labels. Do not render any design explanation or annotations inside the app.
COMPOSITION C — SCENARIO WORKSPACE. A full dashboard shell with a narrow 220px left navigation rail on a subtly cooler surface, and a wide white main workspace. Sidebar top small logo "Idempotent requests lab". Sidebar has a small label "SCENARIOS" then exactly six compact numbered text items: "Send twice", "Lost reply", "Send together", "Fail before saving", "Change content", "Create another". Only second is selected, cobalt-tinted flat rectangle. Sidebar bottom small "2 of 6". In main workspace a compact top bar with "Guided demo" selected and "Technical controls". Below, heading "Lost reply" and one short sentence "The request is saved. The reply never arrives." The center is a broad horizontal REQUEST JOURNEY with three stations connected by fine arrows: "Your screen" monitor with violet "Unconfirmed"; a small middle transit marker "Reply lost"; "Server" with one simple saved ticket labeled "Pump inspection" and green "Saved". Returning arrow points from server towards screen and breaks at the middle; preserve true direction of reply. Beneath journey a slim result strip with "1 send" on left and "1 saved request" on right, no extra charts or widgets. Fixed-looking bottom action bar has a text control "Show explanation" on left and one cobalt button "Retry same request" on right. No other primary buttons. Premium precise alignment, medium-sized task typography, no large repeated descriptions, under 85 visible words including scenario navigation. Useful persistent wayfinding for a presenter, clear content hierarchy. No paragraph, no decorative analytics, no cards around every station.
